LESSON: PEACEFUL CONFLICT RESOLUTION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.5: Peaceful Conflict Resolution

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Peaceful Conflict Resolution. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we promote peace in the community?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions
2. identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives
3. apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PEACEFUL CONFLICT RESOLUTION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Peaceful Conflict Resolution helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: PEACEFUL CONFLICT RESOLUTION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions

What this means
In this part you learn to explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Peaceful Conflict Resolution” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives

What this means
In this part you learn to identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Peaceful Conflict Resolution.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community

What this means
In this part you learn to apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Peaceful Conflict Resolution is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Peaceful Conflict Resolution” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Peaceful Conflict Resolution. (skill: identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Peaceful Conflict Resolution to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions.
3. Practise this skill: identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives.
4. Practise this skill: apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Peaceful Conflict Resolution from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Peaceful Conflict Resolution: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Peaceful Conflict Resolution?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we promote peace in the community?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Peaceful Conflict Resolution means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions.
5. Be able to: identify barriers to conflict resolution in day- to-day lives.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
